title: The normalized Roos fibre computes derived inverse limit with exact products
statement: Let B be an abelian category with countable products, strict inverse limits, exact countable products, and derived categories for B and its strict towers. Suppose the tower category is Grothendieck. Let RF be a functor from the derived category of strict towers to D(B), with a natural comparison η from the ordinary termwise limit followed by Q to Q followed by RF, invertible on every K-injective complex. Form the functorial Roos mapping fibre of minus one-minus-transition, using actual degreewise products of strict tower complexes. There is a natural isomorphism from that fibre followed by Q to Q followed by RF. Its composite with the ordinary-limit kernel inclusion, with zero second coordinate, is exactly η.

source.place: Tags 0940 and 0941; the Roos computation and injective-tower argument

proof.text: Use product projections and tower naturality to construct the Roos fibre functor and the natural kernel comparison from ordinary limit. Its second coordinate is zero.

For a complex of injective strict towers, use the proved split-transition Roos short exact sequence. Negating the final object preserves exactness. The short exact cocone theorem makes its specified kernel inclusion a quasi-isomorphism.

Exact products imply that homology preserves countable products. Product maps and hence the induced cone and shifted fibre maps preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Resolve towers functorially by K-injectives with injective terms. Compose the fibre resolution map, the inverse kernel comparison on the resolution, and η. Naturality cancels the resolution map and proves the normalization.

theorem comparisonIso
    (RF : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B) ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (η : ordinary ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF)
    (hI : ∀ I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B) ℤ, I.IsKInjective → IsIso (η.app I)) :
    ∃ e : fibre ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF,
      Functor.whiskerRight comparison DerivedCategory.Q ≫ e.hom = η
